land.text: the Moche, Chicama and Virú valleys: 'The culture arose about 900 CE, succeeding the Moche culture'

predecessors.note: Dossier moche-culture is written by this group; the Moche are drawn as a culture.

successors.note: Cliopatria's Inca shape takes the coast in 1482; the pages put the conquest in 1470.

capitals.name: Chan Chan (near Trujillo)
capitals.note: Chan Chan page: 'the capital of the historical empire of the Chimor from 900 to 1470'; the city itself 'constructed around 850 AD'; legend credits Taycanamo with founding it.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 911 core shape (2,660 km2) applied to 900-910, the Moche-Chicama-Virú valleys with Chan Chan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Established c. 900' and the text 'The culture arose about 900 CE, succeeding the Moche culture'; Cliopatria's first shape begins in 911. The same core shape is drawn for 900-910.

2,660 km2 round Chan Chan for 911-1176. The page ('centered in the Chicama, Moche, and Viru Valleys') agrees with the core; it gives no area (infobox has none; text: Chimor 'encompassing 1,000 kilometres of ... coastline' at its height, which the 1375 shape matches, see below).

Same 2,660 km2 shape; the split of Cliopatria's rows at 1188 (Chimor to Chimu Empire) is the same state (Wikidata Q581741, one Wikipedia article), so it is one dossier and the shape stands to 1201 unchanged.
Core shape unchanged 1188-1201; no page dates any change in these years.

correction.text: the Moche-Chicama-Virú core only, Jequetepeque not yet conquered: 'The Chimú conquered the Jequetepeque around 1320'

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 6,897 km2 shape reaches the Jequetepeque valley (it holds Pacasmayo) from 1202, but the page says 'The Chimú conquered the Jequetepeque around 1320'. For 1202-1319 the core shape applies; the Cliopatria shape (without its Lambayeque strip) is used from 1320 (next keyframe).

correction.text: the core plus the Jequetepeque valley (Pacasmayo) from c. 1320; Cliopatria's 1202 shape without the Lambayeque-department strip

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1320-1369: Cliopatria's 1202 shape (core plus the Jequetepeque valley), valid from the c. 1320 conquest. The two Lambayeque-side cells (the Zaña valley, the page's 'Sana') are removed until Ñancempinco c. 1370.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 1370-1374 (Ñancempinco's expansion to Zaña, Chao, Santa and on to Carabayllo, 'stopped by the military power of the great valley of Lima')

keyframe_review.note: 43,085 km2 reaching the Casma, Huarmey and Chancay coast south to Carabayllo (Lima department). The page puts the expansion 'both north and south of the Moche Valleys' under Ñancempinco, ruling 'around 1370' (infobox c. 1375), and Carabayllo as the southern limit: so the shape is valid from about 1370, not 1344. Shape unchanged; years 1370-1374.

97,568 km2, Tumbes to Carabayllo: about 920 km of coast, which fits the page's 'encompassing 1,000 kilometres (620 mi) of modern-day Peruvian coastline'. The Lambayeque conquest of 1375 (Lambayeque culture page) matches the shape's start year; Piura and Tumbes are not mentioned by any page opened. Holds through 1470 (not 1474): the Inca conquest is dated 1470.

correction.text: the Chimor coast is Inca land from 1471 (conquest 1470), drawn under inca-empire, not as Chimor

keyframe_review.note: 96,143 km2, the same coast, for 1475-1481: the infobox gives the Inca conquest as 1470 and the Chan Chan page's summary (in the page's words, paraphrased) that Chimor was defeated by the Inca and absorbed into their empire in 1470. Cliopatria's Inca shape takes the coast only in 1482 (it holds all 269 cells of this shape). The land belongs to the Inca from 1471; this shape is not a Chimor shape.

region.text: the Moche, Chicama and Virú valleys round Chan Chan: 'It was centered in the Chicama, Moche, and Viru Valleys'

ledger.note: c. 900: the Chimú arise at Chan Chan in the Moche valley. 'The culture arose about 900 CE, succeeding the Moche culture'; infobox 'Established c. 900'; Chan Chan 'was the capital of the historical empire of the Chimor from 900 to 1470' (Chan Chan page). The page's Chimú oral history gives Taycanamo, who arrives 'from the sea' (infobox c. 1305), and a 'last Chimú kingdom' founded 'in the first half of the fourteenth century'.

region.text: the Jequetepeque valley (Pacasmayo at its mouth)

ledger.counterpart: Jequetepeque valley societies (unnamed on the page)
ledger.note: c. 1320: Chimor conquers the Jequetepeque valley. 'The Chimú conquered the Jequetepeque around 1320 and changed the political structure of the society'; Farfán in the valley became 'a subordinate' of Chan Chan.

region.text: Zaña ('Sana'), Chao and Santa valleys, the new land of Ñancempinco's list

ledger.counterpart: Zaña, Chao and Santa valley societies (unnamed on the page)
ledger.note: c. 1370: Ñancempinco expands Chimor north and south. 'Ñançenpinco began further expansion both north and south of the Moche Valleys' and 'laid the foundations of the Kingdom by conquering ... the neighboring valleys of Sana, Pacasmayo, Chicama, Viru, Chao and Santa'; he 'was believed to have ruled around 1370' (infobox c. 1375). The page's valley list also contains valleys Cliopatria already holds earlier; the new land is Zaña (Sana), Chao and Santa.

region.text: the coast and valleys from Santa south to Carabayllo, Cliopatria's 1344 shape minus its 1202 shape

ledger.note: Chimor reaches Carabayllo on the south. The page says 'To the south, they expanded as far as Carabayllo' and 'Their expansion southward was stopped by the military power of the great valley of Lima' without a date; placed with Ñancempinco, the only expansion the page dates, and with Cliopatria's 1344 shape (page silent on the year).

region.text: the Lambayeque region: the Motupe, La Leche, Lambayeque and Zaña valleys

ledger.note: 1375: Chimor conquers the Sicán heartland of Lambayeque. 'The Late Sican period ... ended with the conquest of the Lambayeque region by the Chimú kingdom of Chimor circa 1375'; 'By the time of the Chimú conquest of the Lambayeque region in 1375'. The Chimor page, by contrast, has the Sicán 'empire' conquering Lambayeque and says Pampa Grande in the Lambayeque valley 'was also ruled by the Chimú'. [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: source changed from the Chimor page, which gives no date for the Lambayeque conquest, to the Lambayeque culture page that the quotes come from]

region.text: the Piura and Tumbes coast north of Lambayeque, Cliopatria's 1375 shape minus its 1344 shape and Lambayeque

ledger.note: The north coast to Tumbes joins Chimor. No page opened mentions Piura or Tumbes; the extent is Cliopatria's 1375 shape, which matches the page's 'encompassing 1,000 kilometres ... of coastline', and the year is the Lambayeque conquest's.

region.text: the whole Chimor coast from Tumbes to Carabayllo

ledger.note: 1470: the Inca take Chimor. Infobox 'Inca conquest 1470'; Chan Chan (paraphrase of its summary): Chimor was defeated and absorbed into the Inca Empire in 1470; the body says 'the Inca conquest began in the 1470s by Topa Inca Yupanqui' and Minchançaman 'was ruling around the time of the Inca conquest (between 1462 and 1470)'. The Topa Inca Yupanqui page says only that he 'conquered Chimor'. Minchançaman was moved to Cusco.

1470: Chimor ends, 'the largest polity conquered by the Inca'; its land goes to the Inca Empire. The page adds that after conquest 'some gained autonomy' and that the Inca conquest was 'nearly complete' only when Huayna Capac took the throne in 1493 (Cliopatria draws the coast as Chimu to 1481 and Inca from 1482).

wars.name: Chimú conquest of the Jequetepeque
wars.outcome: Chimor takes the Jequetepeque valley c. 1320 and reorganises it under Chan Chan, with Farfán as a subordinate centre.
wars.note: The page says 'around 1320' and gives no battle or campaign.

wars.name: Chimú expansion under Ñancempinco
belligerents: valley societies of Zaña, Chao, Santa
wars.outcome: Ñancempinco conquers the valleys north and south of the Moche valley; the southern limit is Carabayllo, where the 'great valley of Lima' stopped Chimor.
wars.note: Dates only by Ñancempinco's rule, 'around 1370' (text) and c. 1375 (infobox).

wars.name: Chimú conquest of Lambayeque
wars.outcome: Chimor conquers the Late Sicán heartland of Lambayeque circa 1375.

wars.name: Inca conquest of Chimor

zones.text: the Chimor coast, Tumbes to Carabayllo

wars.outcome: Topa Inca Yupanqui defeats Minchançaman; Chimor is incorporated into the Inca Empire in 1470 (infobox). Minchançaman goes to Cusco; Chimor's gold and silver 'adorn the Qurikancha'. No contest events are written: no page dates a campaign before the outcome.
wars.note: Dating conflict inside the page: infobox 1470; body 'began in the 1470s' and 'nearly complete' by 1493.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line: the valley limits are the pages' valley names and a coast measured in km; the Lima-valley limit at Carabayllo and the Tumbes limit are the softest.

sources.note: Identity, c. 900 start, 1470 Inca conquest (infobox), rulers, Jequetepeque c. 1320, Ñancempinco c. 1370 and his valleys, Carabayllo, 1,000 km coastline.

notes:
One dossier for Cliopatria's 'Chimor' (911-1187) and 'Chimu Empire' (1188-1481): same Wikidata Q581741 and one Wikipedia article ('Chimor'), which gives no break at 1188. The slug chimu-empire is therefore NOT written separately; chimor reviews all seven shapes of both rows.
Dates that differ from Cliopatria: start 900 (infobox c. 900) against 911; end 1470 (infobox and Chan Chan page) against 1481 (Cliopatria's Inca shape takes the coast in 1482). The page says the Inca conquest 'began in the 1470s' and was 'nearly complete' by 1493: the 1470 end is the infobox's. Founding is soft: Chimú oral history (Taycanamo, infobox c. 1305) and 'the estimated founding date of the last Chimú kingdom ... first half of the fourteenth century' describe a dynasty/kingdom founding that the page does not reconcile with c. 900 for the culture.
Cliopatria shapes adjusted from the page's dates: the Jequetepeque valley is in the shape from 1202 but the page dates its conquest c. 1320 (new keyframe 1320); the 1344 shape (south to Carabayllo) is moved to c. 1370 (Ñancempinco). Both rest on one page's 'around' dates.
Unsettled: the page says Pacasmayo, Chicama, Virú belong to the Ñancempinco list yet also says Jequetepeque fell c. 1320 and the early state was 'centered in the Chicama, Moche, and Viru Valleys' (a contradiction inside the page, kept as is). Piura and Tumbes (north limit) are undated by every page opened. No ruler strip: the infobox lists Taycanamo c. 1305, Wakri Kaur c. 1340, Ñancempinco c. 1375 and Minchançaman c. 1450-c. 1470 (text 1462-1470), with seven unnamed rulers between, which is not a reign list.
Region names the gazetteer may lack: none beyond places used (Pacasmayo, Chimbote exist). The List of wars involving the Inca Empire page has a 'Conquest of the Chimu' in 1470 (agreeing with the infobox) and a 'Rebellion of the Chimu' in 1475 ('Inca victory', the Chimu leader executed); the rebellion falls after the state's end and is kept only as a note here and as a war in the inca-empire dossier. Counterparts without dossiers: the Jequetepeque, Zaña, Chao and Santa valley societies (unnamed); sican-culture and moche-culture are dossiers written by this group.
